characters.name: William Buck
characters.arc: Deputy US Marshal — wants to uphold the law without becoming a tyrant —  — — Active Arc: In Chapter 7, Buck refuses to arrest Rose Aoyama despite having probable cause, choosing to protect the leak over protocol, thereby crossing the line from observer to accomplice.

characters.name: Dalton Voss
characters.arc: Industrialist and antagonist — wants total civic compliance through engineered consent —  — — Active Arc: In Chapter 5, Voss independently negotiates the final water rights purchase using intimidation tactics that Buck did not authorize, demonstrating his willingness to bypass legal channels entirely.

characters.name: Rose Aoyama
characters.arc: Camp engineer and archivist — wants to preserve the truth of the frequency charts —  — — Active Arc: In Chapter 9, Rose deliberately leaves the master tuning key on a workbench in plain sight, forcing Buck’s hand to act before Voss recalibrates the array for Tucson.

characters.name: Sheriff Elias Thorne
characters.arc: Local law enforcement — wants to avoid conflict with Voss to keep Cottonwood Wash prosperous —  — — Active Arc: In Chapter 11, Thorne actively blocks Buck’s attempt to seize the equipment, citing jurisdictional ambiguity, proving that the local establishment has already been compromised.

characters.name: Silas Voss
characters.arc: Dalton’s brother and head of security — wants to eliminate threats to his brother’s project —  — — Active Arc: In Chapter 13, Silas ambushes Buck in the canyon, not to kill him, but to break his favored leg, establishing that Voss prefers crippling over martyrdom.

settings.name: Cottonwood Wash Deputy Office
settings.description: A single-room adobe structure where the desk doubles as a bed; smells of stale tobacco and dried sage, sounds of wind rattling the loose window pane.

settings.name: Voss Construction Camp
settings.description: A fenced perimeter of canvas tents and wooden crates; smells of ozone, hot metal, and unwashed bodies; hums with a low-frequency vibration that rattles teeth.

settings.name: The Aquifer Access Point
settings.description: A concrete-lined well shaft near the riverbank; smells of damp earth and copper; feels slick and cold underfoot.

settings.name: Grissom’s Wells Town Hall
settings.description: A modest wooden hall with peeling paint; smells of dust and old paper; echoes with the unnatural silence of a crowd that has forgotten how to argue.

plot_points.description: Buck observes Voss’s wagons arriving, noting the strange weight of the crates and the lack of standard lumber.
Buck witnesses the first water-rights signing in Grissom’s Wells; the rancher signs willingly, though he previously opposed the sale.
Rose hands Buck the frequency charts, revealing the mechanism of control; Buck realizes the law has no category for this crime.
Buck attempts to arrest Voss, but Sheriff Thorne intervenes, citing federal contracts, leaving Buck powerless and isolated.
Buck infiltrates the main resonance chamber during a storm, realizing Voss is preparing to broadcast the signal to Tucson.
Buck destroys the primary amplifier, causing a feedback loop that shatters the copper pipes and deafens the workers, breaking the spell.
(resolution, ch15) Voss is arrested for the destruction of property, not the coercion; Buck loses his badge for insubordination but saves the territory’s soul.

themes: the cost of order in a lawless land.
voice: Close third-person, past tense; sparse, rhythmic, and grounded in tactile sensation, blending the lean dialogue of Leonard with the moral gravity and elemental imagery of McCarthy.
